subject: Order schedule: price-protection trigger & minimum band proposal
messages:
From: Mara Patel <contracts@orionhealth.com>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@orionhealth.com
Date: 2027-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order schedule: price-protection trigger & minimum band proposal

Irene — thanks for the draft schedule. A couple of quick asks from our side before legal runs a full pass:

1) The 'price-protection' language currently creates a hard floor that would require Orion to commit to a minimum monthly spend for six months before the protection applies. Can you explain the business rationale? That effectively locks us into a band we may not hit.

2) We'd like to propose a simpler mechanism: a rolling 90-day lookback for spikes with a cap on the stabilization credit at 25% of the month’s overage. That keeps spend predictability for us and avoids open-ended credits on your side.

3) Please confirm whether the protection applies to usage on Redwood Dedicated instances or only hosted API. We need clarity for our procurement.

We're attaching the latest order schedule marked with our comments (OrderSchedule_v3.docx). If you can send a redline with alternatives (net-new clause and the rolling-lookback variant), we'll route to our CPO/legal.

Best,
Mara
Mara Patel
Senior Contracts Manager, Orion Health

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Mara Patel <contracts@orionhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order schedule: price-protection trigger & minimum band proposal

Mara — thanks for the clear asks. High-level responses below and next steps at the bottom.

1) Why the floor: the original intent was to protect against severe step-downs in average unit economics when customers transition heavy production traffic between model families. Practically that prevents runaway unit-cost variance for both sides. That said, the six-month hard minimum is heavier than necessary for your use case.

2) Rolling 90-day lookback: we can provide that as an alternative. Two design choices: (A) rolling lookback with a stabilization credit capped at 25% of the month's overage (as you propose); or (B) a smoothing corridor where month-to-month overage beyond a 20% delta triggers a capped credit. Option A aligns with your ask.

3) Scope (Hosted vs Dedicated): protection applies to hosted API and Redwood Dedicated by default unless you elect to exclude Dedicated in which case pricing is governed by the Dedicated SOW. We can spell this out explicitly to avoid ambiguity.

Next steps: I'm looping in Laura from legal to produce two tracked-redline alternatives: (1) "rolling-lookback" variant that matches your cap request and (2) a lighter "corridor" variant that preserves some minimum commitment but with faster decay (90 days). Karthik — can you confirm the commercial concession we can offer for the rolling-lookback option (target concession in $ or %)? I want to surface that in the redline.

I'll get the redline to you by EOD Thursday.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Order schedule: price-protection trigger & minimum band proposal

Mara / team — quick commercial note from my side.

We can accept the rolling 90-day lookback with a 25% stabilization-credit cap as a one-time concession tied to a 12-month committed ARR band. Concession outline:
- If Orion signs a 12-month order schedule at the attached tiered banding, Redwood will include the rolling-lookback protector and cap at 25%.
- If Orion later expands to Dedicated capacity, the protector remains in effect for hosted consumption only; Dedicated will be covered under the Dedicated SOW pricing.

I propose a trade: we include the rolling-lookback language (your ask) if Orion confirms the 12-month commit (we can finalize exact ARR numbers in the order schedule). That gives us predictability and keeps the credit exposure bounded.

Happy to jump on a 20-min call to close this if helpful.

— Karthik
VP, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Mara Patel <contracts@orionhealth.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-28T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order schedule: price-protection trigger & minimum band proposal

Mara — attaching a redline with two options as promised (see attached: ORN-321-Protector-Excerpt.pdf and OrderSchedule_v3.docx with tracked changes). Key notes on the language so you have context: 

1) Rolling-lookback variant (Option A):
- "Price Protection" will be calculated on a rolling 90-day period; stabilization credits are capped at 25% of the monthly overage.
- Credits are applied as a reduction to the following billing cycle and cannot be converted to cash.
- The clause explicitly excludes Dedicated SOW charges unless both Parties execute an addendum.

2) Smoothing-corridor variant (Option B):
- If month-over-month usage increases by more than 20% relative to the 90-day average, Redwood will apply a stabilization allowance capped at 20% and applied over two subsequent billing cycles.
- This variant preserves a modest minimum commitment: if average monthly billed units fall below 60% of the contracted band for two consecutive months, the Parties will reconcile via true-up or rebaseline within 30 days.

3) Carve-outs and limits: both options include an explicit exclusion for proof-of-concept or trial environment usage, and a force-majeure carve-out for cloud regional outages.

4) Operational: please confirm which billing contact we should use for credit application and whether you want credits demonstrated as line items (we recommend visible line-item credits for auditability).

If Orion prefers Option A (rolling-lookback), Karthik's commercial concession (12-month commitment) should be added as a Subscriber Commitment paragraph. Once you confirm, we'll circulate a clean and a tracked final for signature (DocuSign link will be sent).

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: OrderSchedule_v3.docx (comments), ORN-321-Protector-Excerpt.pdf (tracked redline)
